about.title: California City Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: California City sits along industrial and commercial corridors near California City Boulevard and Rt 58, where warehouse work, delivery routes, construction, and municipal jobs bring daily physical risk. When a worker is hurt on the job here, California's workers' compensation system usually becomes the exclusive remedy against the employer, no matter who was at fault. But that system doesn't cover everything, and it doesn't apply to everyone who contributed to the harm. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on a road like Neuralia Road or Randsburg Mojave Road played a role in your injury, a separate third-party claim may be available alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive connects injured workers in California City with an independent attorney, free of charge, to help sort out which paths apply. There's never a fee unless a recovery is made.

whyChoose.title: Why Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Identify Third-Party Responsibility
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the only remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can support a separate claim. An independent attorney can look at your situation to see if that applies.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Getting connected early helps avoid missed windows.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Are Real
items.desc: California law prohibits retaliation against workers for reporting an on-the-job injury. An independent attorney can help you understand your rights if you're worried about how a report might be received.

items.question: Can I file a workplace injury claim if I already have a workers' comp case open?
items.answer: Yes, in many situations a third-party claim can proceed separately from your workers' compensation case. Workers' comp usually covers the employer relationship, while a third-party claim addresses a different negligent party. An independent attorney can review both to see how they fit together.

items.question: I was injured working near California City Boulevard while driving for my job. Does that count as a workplace injury?
items.answer: It can. Work-related driving injuries, including collisions on corridors like California City Boulevard or Rt 58, are often handled through workers' compensation first, but if another driver was at fault, a separate third-party claim may also be possible. An independent attorney can help sort out which claims apply to your situation.

items.question: What if my employer told me not to report my injury?
items.answer: California law protects workers from retaliation for reporting a workplace injury, and generally requires that a report be made within 30 days. If you were discouraged from reporting, it's worth speaking with an independent attorney about your options before that window closes.
